questions.question: Discuss on the main concern of metaphysics / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Metaphysics concerns the fundamental nature of reality - focusing on existence, being,
  • causality, and the relationship between mind and matter -seeks to understand what lies
  • beyond the physical world and what constitutes ultimate reality
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Briefly explain the concept of the General Will in Rousseau's political thought. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Rousseau’s concept of the General Will represents the collective interest of the citizens
  • aimed at the common good -transcends individual desires, guiding laws and governance to
  • ensure freedom and equality within the social contract.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How is authority different from power? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Authority is legitimate power accepted by those it governs, based on consent or law -
  • power, by contrast, refers to the ability to influence or control others’ behaviour, which may
  • exist without legitimacy or moral justification.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does the World Bank help in poverty alleviation? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• The World Bank aids poverty alleviation by funding development projects, promoting
  • education, healthcare, and infrastructure, and supporting economic reforms - provides
  • technical expertise and low -interest loans to help developing nations build sustainable
  • growth.

questions.question: Examine the limitations of Political Philosophy / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Political philosophy is limited by its abstract nature, cultural biases, and distance from
  • practical politics-its idealistic assumptions may overlook power dynamics, economic realities,
  • and historical conditions influencing real political processes.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does Gandhiji correlate civil disobedience and moral obligation to disobey unjust laws? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Gandhi viewed civil disobedience as a moral duty to resist unjust laws peacefully- believed
  • individuals must follow conscience and truth (satyagraha), asserting that moral obligation to
  • justice overrides obedience to oppressive authority.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Evaluate the challenges of realizing justice in pluralistic societies. How do normative frameworks attempt to reconcile liberty, equality, and fairness / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• In pluralistic societies, justice faces challenges due to cultural diversity, conflicting values,
  • and social inequalities -normative frameworks like Rawls’s justice as fairness and
  • multicultural models strive to balance liberty, equality, and fairness inclusively.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Critically evaluate the justification of political authority proposed by Marselius of Padua. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Marsilius of Padua justified political authority through the collective will of the people,
  • rejecting papal supremacy-emphasized secular governance and popular sovereignty, though
  • critics argue his model underestimates moral and spiritual authority.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Analyze cultural cosmopolitanism in the context of migration. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Cultural cosmopolitanism promotes global citizenship, emphasizing openness, diversity,
  • and shared human values amid migration -values hybrid identities and mutual respect but
  • faces challenges from nationalism, inequality, and cultural assimilation pressures.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the main principles of governance. / [CO2] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Principles of governance include accountability, ensuring leaders answer to the public -
  • transparency, maintaining openness in decision -making- participation, involving citizens in
  • governance; rule of law, ensuring justice; and responsiveness to public needs.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Examine the role of political Philosophy in everyday politics / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Political philosophy guides everyday politics by shaping moral and ethical standards for
  • governance, citizenship, and justice-influences public debates, policymaking, and democratic
  • participation by offering frameworks to evaluate authority, rights, and collective welfare in
  • practical political contexts
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the different forms and dimensions of equality. How do they interact with the principles of liberty and justice in modern political theory? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Equality includes political, social, and economic dimensions ensuring fair opportunities
  • and treatment -political equality secures participation rights, social equality promotes
  • inclusion, and economic equality reduces disparities -these forms interact with liberty and
  • justice by balancing individual freedom with fairness and collective well-being.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Briefly discuss the various theories on the nature of the State. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Theories on the nature of the state include idealist, realist, liberal, and Marxist views -
  • Idealists see the state as a moral institution - realists emphasize power and security - liberals
  • view it as a social contract ensuring rights -Marxists see it as a tool of class domination -
  • feminist theory critiques patriarchy and demands gender equality in power structures-social
  • contract theory sees the state as formed by individuals’ consent for mutual protection-divine
  • origin views it as God -given-evolutionary emphasizes gradual developme nt-force theory
  • bases it on coercion.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Do you think that sovereignty should be redefined in the era of globalization? / [CO4] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• In globalization, sovereignty requires redefinition due to interdependence among states,
  • global governance institutions, and transnational challenges -while absolute sovereignty
  • weakens, cooperative sovereignty emerges, balancing national autonomy with international
  • responsibility and collective action for global justice and security.
